chairs.author: Bernays, Propaganda 1928
chairs.face: the polite man who explains that the war is a service

telling.text: You arrived at the Wall expecting one of two service tiers, and the Wall politely declined both factions' passes and offered no fight; the stone plainly states the fence has two sides: neither force the end, nor flee from it. There is a toll, and there is a walk-away option, both administered at the desk. Should you attempt the forced climb at maximum war rank, you will incur the FAILED DATE condition, which suspends boon drafts until any Door riddle attempt, right or wrong; the complimentary DON'T PANIC towel also resolves it, and we appreciate your continued consent.

At the river ford north you will find the glass door into the keep of clear pipes; admission is two dice, pass on seven, a standard rate already used across the property. The first riddle supplies the answer, 42, and requests the question, an exchange we find highly efficient; the second asks you to identify a ten-day-darkness forecast welded onto real EAS alert infrastructure, so simply name the weld and demand the receipt. The third riddle remains reserved for the Riddler endgame cohort, and we assure you the reservation is itself a service.

The middle path is not a third faction; it is the same two audiences, consented rather than commanded, and your chair unlocks the Temple Broadcast at Act III eligibility. You author counter-media and the faction sentiment meters actually move, which is persuasion made honest at last: Act I is only honest if you can become a propagandist too. Resolution remains two dice, pass on seven; nothing about the arrangement changes except whose message is playing.

chairs.mechanic_hook: Sitting unlocks THE TEMPLE BROADCAST at Act III eligibility: the daily faction sentiment meter made real, plus the counter-media editor; your authored media measurably moves the meters (falsifier F5).

chairs.author: Ellul, The Technological Society 1964
chairs.face: the tired technician who loves nothing

telling.text: The Wall is a technique, not an adversary: both faction passes are refused as inputs and no combat subroutine is offered, the stone reading ASCEND NOT AS A WALL, a fence with two sides where forcing and fleeing are the two error states. The toll is paid or the walk option is taken; those are the only sanctioned exits. A forced climb at maximum war rank triggers FAILED DATE and suspends boon drafts until any Door riddle attempt, correct or not; the DON'T PANIC towel is the approved countermeasure.

The Door stands at the river ford north, a glass interface into the keep of clear pipes, opening on 2d6, pass on 7, the same threshold that integrates all resolution in this system. Riddle one returns the answer 42 and demands the question; riddle two requires the solver to identify a ten-day-darkness forecast welded onto real EAS alert infrastructure and to demand the receipt for the weld; riddle three is unallocated, reserved by contract for the Riddler endgame cohort. Technique absorbs the riddle as it absorbs everything; the only open question is whether the solver can still tell an anchor from a weld.

The middle path is not a synthesis; it is the refusal of both total methods, and at Act III eligibility your chair exposes the Inefficiency Ledger. The Vow costs, the Seed wastes, the Pilgrim sheds loot, and no optimization path may exist: the moment a meta min-maxes faith, the house has absorbed the Third Way and the mechanic is re-priced. Resolution stays 2d6, pass on 7; the dice do not optimize either.

chairs.mechanic_hook: Sitting unlocks the Inefficiency Ledger at Act III eligibility: the priced cost of the Vow, the Seed's waste, the Pilgrim's shed loot, and the re-price trigger that fires when a meta optimizes faith (falsifier F6).

chairs.author: LeGuin, The Ones Who Walk Away from Omelas 1973; The Dispossessed 1974
chairs.face: the one who is not at home in either city

telling.text: The Wall turned both factions away, and it would not fight you; the stone says a fence has two sides, that you may not force the end and you may not flee from it either. There was a toll to pay and a road that walks away, and you could take either without lying down. Climb it in fury at the height of the war and you will carry FAILED DATE, your boon drafts gone dark, until some honest attempt at a Door riddle, right or wrong, lifts it; the DON'T PANIC towel will hold you till then.

North at the river ford there is a glass door into the keep of clear pipes, and it opens on two dice, on a seven, no more and no less than the town's own luck. The first riddle gives you the answer, 42, and asks you for the question, which is the way of doors; the second asks who welded a ten-day-darkness forecast onto the real alert lines, and the answer is to name the weld and demand the receipt. The third riddle is not written yet: it belongs to the Riddler endgame cohort, who must author it before Act III widens, and an unwritten riddle is still an honest one.

The middle path is not the pleasant road between two cities; it is the city you can only have by refusing both of these. At Act III eligibility the Walker's price is named: the endgame must find the child, the shared VM pool fed by both factions' kills, and cut the treadmill at its source, for every player, dark, light, and pilgrim alike. An exit that leaves the city as it was is Omelas with extra steps, and resolution stays what it always was: two dice, pass on seven.

chairs.mechanic_hook: Sitting unlocks the Walker's Price at Act III eligibility: the endgame contract to find the child and cut the VM treadmill at its source, abolishing the pool for every player (falsifier F7).

chairs.author: Vonnegut, Slaughterhouse-Five 1969
chairs.face: the man who has seen his own death and is fine about it

telling.text: The Wall refused both factions and offered no fight, and the stone said a fence has two sides, no forcing and no fleeing, and that was that. Billy paid the toll, or he walked away, or he climbed it on the day the war was biggest and got the FAILED DATE, and his boon drafts went dark, so it goes. A towel that says DON'T PANIC took it off, or any riddle attempt did, right or wrong; he was unstuck, not blessed.

The Door is at the river ford north, glass, into a keep of clear pipes, and it opens on two dice when you roll a seven, which some moments you do and some moments you have already done. The first riddle tells you the answer is 42 and asks for the question, and there is no hurry, since all the moments are there at once. The second wants you to notice a ten-day-darkness forecast welded onto the real alert lines and to ask for the receipt, and the third is reserved for the Riddler endgame cohort, who arrive later in the book.

The middle path is not a prize; the saint of the third way is the unpanicked man, not the rewarded one. At Act III eligibility your chair says so it goes, every death, right in the death text, and the shared respawn is being unstuck, never being blessed. Two dice, pass on seven, all of it happening somewhere in the middle where nobody forced anything and nobody ran.

chairs.mechanic_hook: Sitting unlocks SO IT GOES at Act III eligibility: the Pilgrim's death line, every death, and shared respawn narrated as unstuck, never as blessing.

chairs.author: Adams, The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy 1979
chairs.face: the cheerful voice that knows everything and believes nothing

telling.text: The Wall has refused both faction passes, declined to fight anyone, and put up a stone that says a fence has two sides: neither force the end, nor flee from it, which is technically complete and no help whatsoever at the bottom of a wall. There is a toll and a walk-away option, both suspiciously reasonable. Climb it in anger at the top of the war and you collect FAILED DATE, a small grey cloud that switches off your boon drafts; a towel printed DON'T PANIC cancels it, and so does trudging off to attempt any Door riddle, even badly.

The Door is north at the river ford, made of glass, leading into a keep of clear pipes, and it opens on two dice at seven or better, improbability here being strictly rationed. Riddle one hands you the answer, 42, and asks for the question, which everyone agrees is the annoying part; riddle two asks you to spot a ten-day-darkness forecast welded onto real EAS alert infrastructure and demand the receipt, which is always the correct thing to demand. Riddle three is reserved for the Riddler endgame cohort, who are presumably still looking for it.

The middle path is the arrangement in which nobody has forcibly ended anything and nobody has fled, and everyone is faintly disappointed, which is how you know it is working. At Act III eligibility your chair rents the Improbability Drive: grace rolls spend a visible Improbability resource, because luck in this establishment is a spent thing, not a free one, and the peeked version is the Finite Improbability Generator, which burns its users. The DON'T PANIC towel is on sale, resolution stays two dice, pass on seven, and the answer remains 42 pending receipt of the question.

chairs.mechanic_hook: Sitting unlocks the Improbability Drive at Act III eligibility: grace rolls spend visible Improbability, the peeked Finite Improbability Generator burns its users, and the DON'T PANIC towel counters the despair debuff.

chairs.author: Pratchett, Small Gods 1992; Hogfather 1996; the Discworld
chairs.face: the tortoise in the corner of the tavern who is God
chairs.register_note: only this chair may use a CAPS Death-style aside; exactly one is used, in the Act III beat

telling.text: There was once a Wall that had refused both factions by teatime and out-waited a hundred heroes, every one of whom had explained, right up to the walling, that they were the exception. The stone upon it said a fence has two sides, and that you shall not force the end nor flee from it, which is the oldest kind of law, carved where the climbing boots go; there was a toll, and a road that walked away, for those who preferred their doors unfought. Those who forced the climb, at the very height of the war, wore FAILED DATE like a collar, boon drafts gone dark, until a towel that said DON'T PANIC, or one honest shove at a Door riddle, right or wrong, took it off again.

North at the river ford stands a door made of glass into a keep of clear pipes, and it opens to two dice and a seven, because doors, like gods, run on what the world actually believes. The first riddle hands you 42 and asks for the question, which is the universe's oldest bit and still gets a laugh; the second asks you to see the weld where a ten-day-darkness forecast was stuck onto the real alert lines, and to demand the receipt, because belief spent on welded things is belief wasted. The third riddle is not written, and is waiting for the Riddler endgame cohort to arrive and take the blame.

The middle path is the story nobody tells at the temples, and it rolls the same two dice, pass on seven, that every door in this world uses. At Act III eligibility your chair wakes the belief meters, and a god with one true believer is a tortoise while a god with ten thousand is a thunderbolt, and the tortoise in the corner of the Guttered Lantern, the one everyone steps around, is the endgame and is listening. THE VOW IS THE SMALL-LIES GYM, WHERE YOU PRACTICE BELIEVING ON BOON DRAFTS BEFORE ANYTHING LARGE ASKS.

chairs.mechanic_hook: Sitting unlocks the Small Gods belief meters at Act III eligibility: the three boon-card gods grow with player belief over time, and the corner tortoise of the Guttered Lantern is revealed as the endgame NPC.
